name: free
description: Shows total, used, and free physical memory and swap.

examples.output:
total   used   free   shared  buff/cache  available
Mem:    15Gi  3.0Gi  8.2Gi    210Mi       4.1Gi      11Gi
Swap:  2.0Gi     0B  2.0Gi
examples.explanation: The important column is "available" (11Gi) — memory that applications can actually claim. "free" being small is normal and healthy: Linux uses spare RAM for caching.
Refreshes every 2 seconds to watch memory trends. Ctrl+C to stop.

about: Linux borrows unused RAM for disk cache (buff/cache) and returns it instantly when applications need it. Therefore: low "free" is normal; low "available" is the real warning. Swap in use with plenty of available memory is also normal (old pages moved out); continuous heavy swap-in/out (thrashing) means you need more RAM.
mistakes: Panic over low "free" memory — read "available" instead.
Adding up used+free and expecting the total; buff/cache is the difference.
